title: Anthropic Licenses $300M Opaque Systems Tech to Process Sensitive AI Data
summary:
Aaron Fulkerson and Rishabh Poddar are among the staff members joining Anthropic to deploy AI tools in hospitals and banks. Through a new acquihire and licensing deal, Anthropic has hired several employees from the security startup Opaque Systems, including its CEO and CTO, to adopt a platform that runs AI jobs inside hardware sealed environments. This technology produces cryptographic evidence of every run to verify how sensitive records are handled, closing a security gap where data is typically vulnerable after being decrypted in memory.

Opaque Systems was valued at $300M following a $24M Series B in February and has raised $55.5M in total funding since originating as a UC Berkeley RISELab project about 10 years ago. Anthropic was previously a customer of the startup and had published a confidential inference design with Pattern Labs in June 2025. It is not yet known if Opaque Systems will continue serving existing clients, such as Accenture and ServiceNow, under the new structure.

selectedTweets.text:
Anthropic's new acqui-hire deal. 

Its licensing Opaque Systems’ technology for running AI on confidential data and hiring some of its engineers, including CEO Aaron Fulkerson and CTO Rishabh Poddar.

> Standard encryption guards data on disk and across networks, but a model can only read it once it’s decrypted in memory.
> Opaque’s platform closes that gap by running AI jobs inside hardware-sealed environments that produce cryptographic evidence of what happened during each run.
> That evidence lets a bank or hospital verify which code touched its records, on which machine and under which rules.

That technology began as a UC Berkeley RISELab project about 10 years ago and carried Opaque to a $300M valuation after a $24M Series B in February, with $55.5M raised in total.

Anthropic was already an Opaque customer and had published a confidential inference design with Pattern Labs in June 2025, while noting that some AI chips still lack full confidential computing support.

Neither company has said whether Opaque’s platform will keep serving ServiceNow, Accenture and its other customers under the license-and-hire structure.
